Public Portion 
 1. Discussion and Review of the Vehicle Replacement Plan. 
 
Minutes: 
On September 29, 2026, the Joint Maintenance & Development and Finance Committees, 
chaired by Councilor Lavar Click-Bruce, met to review the City’s Vehicle Replacement Plan. 
Present were Councilors Maria Perez and Victor Davila, CAFO Cathy Buono, DPW Director 
Chris Cignoli, and Deputy CAFO Lindsey Hackett. The plan provides a comprehensive review 
of the City’s approximately 883 vehicles and pieces of equipment and establishes a five-year 
replacement schedule based on age, mileage, condition, operational needs, and estimated 
replacement costs. 
 
The proposed first-year purchase includes 73 vehicles at an estimated cost of $6 million, 
including 36 Police Department vehicles, 7 Fire Department vehicles, 24 General Fund vehicles, 
and 6 Enterprise Fund vehicles. The City plans to seek a $6 million bond authorization for the 
purchases. Departments worked together to prioritize replacement needs, and the City will make 
purchases through state contracts and its procurement process. The committee also reviewed 
Police and Fire vehicle needs, DPW equipment, street sweepers, trash trucks, snow removal 
equipment, trade-ins, and the use of Chapter 90 funding for certain DPW purchases. The Vehicle 
Replacement Plan is expected to be updated approximately every two years to reflect changes in 
fleet conditions, operational needs, and costs. 
 
No recommendation was made. The Vehicle Replacement Plan and proposed bond authorization 
will proceed to the Finance Committee for further review before consideration by the full City 
Council. The Vehicle Replacement Plan was reviewed, and copies were to be distributed to City 
Councilors.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 4:39 p.m.
